clean_story:
"Sound made by machines. Music shaped by electricity.

The term electronic music comes from its source: sounds created or changed using electronic devices, like synthesizers or computers.

Most people think of it as just beats and loops, but it starts with raw voltage. A synthesizer turns electricity into sound waves, the way a radio turns them back into music. In 1964, Robert Moog built the first modular synthesizer, letting musicians sculpt sound like clay. Wendy Carlos used it to play Bach on Switched-On Bach, proving machines could make music as warm as any orchestra. Today, a laptop can do what once needed a room of gear, turning knobs and sliders into code. Yet the core stays the same: shaping electricity into emotion.

Three related subjects are sound synthesis, digital audio workstations and music production."
